dialogue.Introduction: Oh. A customer. Or a visitor. Either way, mind the mannequins, they are expensive and I am bad-tempered.$u#$b#I am the Clothier. Skeletron himself cursed me and dragged me up here to stitch hats for strangers, so you will forgive me if I skip the warm welcome.$s
dialogue.Mon: Monday again. I air out the hats every week. Dust is the enemy of good fabric and of bad memories.
dialogue.Tue: The Stylist keeps telling me to smile more. I told her a grimace is simply a strong opinion about cloth.
dialogue.Wed: On Wednesdays the caravan brings wool from the Forest. I check every bolt twice. The curse ruined my trust in anything with a dark lining.
dialogue.Thu: Thursday. I spend my mornings wondering whether the Old Man in the dungeon is still waiting to be rescued. Not by me, mind.
dialogue.Fri: Fridays the miners bring up silk from the caves. It is the only good thing the mines have ever given me.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday, and the Stylist is off gossiping in the Stardrop Saloon again. Somebody has to keep the shop running, and that somebody is me.
dialogue.Sun: Sundays I rest. Or I try to. The sewing machine has a mind of its own on the day of rest.
dialogue.Mon2: Oh, you again. Do you want a hat, or do you just enjoy standing in my shop looking at the hats?
dialogue.Wed2: Hm. Your cloak has a loose seam. I can see it from here. Do not argue with the tailor.
dialogue.Fri2: Come in, come in, but wipe your boots. Those caves left me with a very strong dislike of mud.
dialogue.Sun2: Sunday visitors are rare. Most of Pelican Town still thinks I am glaring at them from some dark cave.
dialogue.Mon4: You are becoming a regular. I suppose I should start saving a chair for you by the stove.$h
dialogue.Tue4: Most people only come in for a shirt. You come in to talk. I am not sure what to make of that yet.$h
dialogue.Wed4: Before the curse I dreamed of being a great warrior. Now I dream of the perfect buttonhole.$s
dialogue.Thu4: The sun was out and I actually enjoyed the walk to the beach yesterday. Do not tell the Stylist I said so.$h
dialogue.Fri4: The miners never ask for a proper collar, but they should. I am trying to change that, one stitch at a time.$h
dialogue.Sat4: Saturday is my only day to take a breath. I think I will spend it with you, if you do not mind the grumbling.$h
dialogue.Sun4: I have not been this comfortable on a Sunday in years. The curse feels further away when you are around.$l
dialogue.Mon8: Do you know what this shop was before the curse? A place to hide. Now it is a place I am glad to have.$s
dialogue.Tue8: I am still ashamed of some of the things I did under the curse. You have seen the worst of my temper, and you still come back.$s
dialogue.Wed8: If I am honest, I was afraid you would stop coming once you found out what a grump I really am.$s
dialogue.Thu8: Would you like to know my secret? I still sew my best hats while thinking of you. Do not let it go to your head.$l
dialogue.Fri8: The miners say I am the crossest tailor in the valley. I do not mind. You never seemed to mind, which is why I trust you.$h
dialogue.Sat8: I want you to know, @, that you are the only person who has ever made this shop feel like a home.$l
dialogue.Sun8: Sundays with you are my favourite now. No dungeon, no curse, just a warm stove and good company.$l
dialogue.danceRejection: I am not ready to dance in front of the whole valley yet. Ask me again later. The curse made me a terrible dancer.$s
dialogue.Tue6: You kept your word and came back. I trust the stitching of people who keep their word.$h
dialogue.Thu6: The Stylist and I argued about curtain colours. I won, obviously, but I felt guilty afterwards.$s
dialogue.Sat6: Some days I feel like the curse is only sleeping. You make that feeling easier to ignore.$h
dialogue.Fri10: @, if I could choose any companion in the valley, I would still choose you.$l
dialogue.Sun10: I have sewn you a little scarf. It is nothing special. It is simply the best thing I have ever made.$l
dialogue.Thu10: When you walk into the room I forget how to hold my pins. It is quite embarrassing for a tailor.$l
dialogue.Sat10: I used to think love was only for the lucky. Maybe I was just unlucky until you walked into my shop.$l
dialogue.spring_Wed: Spring rain makes the fabric damp. Still, the shop smells of flowers and I cannot complain.$h
dialogue.summer_Sat: Summer heat is terrible for wool. I have taken to wearing linen like some sort of coastal dandy.$h
dialogue.fall_Mon: Autumn is when the Fair comes round. I always enter a waistcoat and always lose to the Stylist.$a
dialogue.winter_Thu: Winter nights are long and cold. I have been doing extra stitching to keep the shop warm.$h
dialogue.fall_15: The leaves are falling and I am behind on orders. Do not look so smug, you have not even paid yet.$h
dialogue.winter_12: The snow makes everything quiet. Even the dungeon feels far away in this weather.$s
dialogue.spring_6: Spring cleaning. I have thrown out three moth-eaten coats and one pair of cursed gloves. Good riddance.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: Friday nights in winter are my favourite. We sit by the stove and I pretend to be grumpy about it.$l

rainy: Rain on the shop roof. Good for sewing, bad for the old curse ache in my bones.$s

marriage.Indoor_Day_0: It is a fine afternoon indoors, @. I am pinning a hem and trying not to glare at the sunlight.
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: Careful with the pins, @. Oh, you are grinning. Stop it. I am trying to work.$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: The house feels right with you in it. Hand me that spool, would you?$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: Sometimes I catch myself humming. The Stylist says it is alarming. I think it is lovely.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: I stitched a little patch on your coat. Do not tell anyone it is shaped like a heart. It is a heart.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: The rain is drumming on the roof. Good weather for sewing and for sitting close.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: Rain again. My old bones ache in it, but I do not mind when you put a blanket on my knees.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: Listen to that rain, @. It sounds like a hundred tiny needles. I rather like it.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: Leave the shop shut today. The rain and I are both grumpy, so we will sit together and be grumpy.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: I am glad you came home before the storm. The house feels safe with you in it.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: The lamps are low and the house is quiet. Do not stay up too late, @, you look tired.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: I could not sleep, so I came down. You followed me, I suppose. Come and sit by the stove.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: Good night, @. I will put the lamp out in a minute. Just one more stitch.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: Goodness, it is late. Do not look at me like that. Fine, one more story, then bed.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: At night I used to think of the dungeon. Now I think of your hands on my shoulders. Much better.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: Rain on the shop windows at night. Lovely. Let us stay inside and pretend the outside does not exist.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: The curse never liked rainy nights. You have made them a little easier, @.$s
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: Listen to the drumming. It sounds like someone knocking to be let in. Good thing I already let you in.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: Keep the blanket tonight. I am perfectly warm right here beside you.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: I love the sound of rain on the roof when you are beside me. Do not tell the Stylist I said that.$l
marriage.Outdoor_0: A walk outside, @? Keep your hat on. The sun here is far too bright for my taste.$h
marriage.Outdoor_1: The valley looks lovely from here. I thought I would hate the outdoors forever. I was wrong.$h
marriage.Outdoor_2: Hold my arm on the path, @. The stones are uneven and I would rather not fall in front of the mayor.$h
marriage.Outdoor_3: Look at the sky. There is no dungeon in it, just clouds and gulls over the beach.$s
marriage.Outdoor_4: I am so glad we took the long way round today. Every step is one I did not spend in that cave.$l
marriage.Good_0: Good morning, my dear. Your coffee is on the stove. Do not burn your tongue.$h
marriage.Good_1: You look well today, @. Stand still a moment, I want to see the colour back in your cheeks.$h
marriage.Good_2: Today I feel like a proper tailor again. Thank you for being here to see it.$h
marriage.Good_3: I have a new idea for the shop. A coat in every colour in the valley, and you will model every one.$h
marriage.Good_4: Do you know what I like best about you? You always come back after a hard day.$h
marriage.Good_5: You are a good partner, @. Do not let anyone tell you otherwise.$h
marriage.Good_6: This morning I was up before the sun. I think I was only waiting to see you wake up.$l
marriage.Good_7: The kitchen smells lovely. I may have burnt the bread, but the company was perfect.$h
marriage.Good_8: You fixed the leaky roof without my asking. That is the sort of thing that makes an old grump melt.$l
marriage.Good_9: Every day I am glad the Old Man sent me to stitch hats in a valley full of people like you.$l
marriage.Neutral_0: Morning, @. The bread is stale and I have a hem to finish. Pass the jam.
marriage.Neutral_1: You left your boots by the door again. Honestly, @, I am not your servant.$a
marriage.Neutral_2: I am busy today. Do not expect the same smile you get on a Sunday.$s
marriage.Neutral_3: We need more thread. Could you pick some up from the Stylist? She will only charge you double.$a
marriage.Neutral_4: Oh, it is you. Hm. Well, make yourself useful and hold this pattern.$u
marriage.Neutral_5: I did not sleep well. The curse was grumbling in my bones again. Try not to take it personally.$s
marriage.Neutral_6: Yes, yes, I heard you. The shop is open and the lamp is lit. Now please let me work.$a
marriage.Neutral_7: The cat knocked over a whole spool of silk. Do not look at me like that, it was not my fault.$a
marriage.Neutral_8: I cannot find my good scissors anywhere. Check the cupboard, I am sure you moved them.$a
marriage.Neutral_9: Fine. You can stay. But stop whistling, it is ruining my concentration.$h
marriage.Bad_0: Do not talk to me before I have had my tea. You know the rule.$a
marriage.Bad_1: The shop has been a mess all morning. I am sorry for snapping at you, but I cannot seem to stop.$s
marriage.Bad_2: Honestly, @, I had hoped for a quiet day. I am tired and everything I wear is itchy.$a
marriage.Bad_3: Leave the pins where they are. If you touch them I will have to start all over again.$a
marriage.Bad_4: I am not in the mood to be cheerful today. Go and bother the Stylist for an hour.$a
marriage.Bad_5: The cold got into my bones last night. I am cross, and you are here, so you get the cross end of me.$a
marriage.Bad_6: No, I do not want to hear about the goblins again. I have had enough goblins for a lifetime.$a
marriage.Bad_7: Stop sighing at me. I am sighing at myself, and that is quite enough sighing for one house.$a
marriage.Bad_8: I know I am grumpy. I am working on it, I promise. Just give me a little space today.$s
marriage.Bad_9: I do not hate you. I hate this coat, which is ruined, and I hate that I cannot fix it.$s
marriage.OneKid_0: Look at you, @, with %kid1 on your hip. I never pictured it. Our little one is far too clever.$h
marriage.OneKid_1: %kid1 has taken my scissors again. The child has a talent for theft, and I am so proud.$h
marriage.OneKid_2: Do not let %kid1 near the silk. Last time a whole bolt ended up as a cape on the cat.$h
marriage.OneKid_3: %kid1 asked me if the curse could be undone. I said yes, with love and good stitching. Pure nonsense, of course.$l
marriage.TwoKids_0: Between %kid1 and %kid2 this house is a circus. I would not trade it for all the silk in the valley.$h
marriage.TwoKids_1: %kid2 wants a hat like mine. %kid1 wants a sword. I told them both that is not how it works.$h
marriage.TwoKids_2: Hush, %kid1, %kid2 is sleeping. Honestly, you two make more noise than the mines.$h
marriage.TwoKids_3: The children have started calling me Papa Grump. I think I like it more than I should.$l
marriage.NoBed_0: There is a little bed missing from the back room, @. It is not a problem. We will find space somewhere.$s
marriage.NoBed_1: The spare room is cold and damp. Maybe we should think about a bigger house someday.$s
marriage.NoBed_2: We have no spare bed yet. Do not worry. The couch is wide enough for both of us, I promise.$h
marriage.NoBed_3: One day we will have room for a crib. Until then the sewing basket makes an excellent bed for the cat.$h
marriage.patio_Emily: The patio is a lovely spot for a morning drink, @. Come out and sit with me.$h
marriage.spouseRoom_Emily: I hung a new curtain in our room. It is blue, because you said you liked blue. Do not argue.$l
marriage.funLeave_Emily: I am off to the shop for the day, @. Keep the stove warm and do not let the Stylist steal my pins.$h
marriage.funReturn_Emily: I am back, @. Let me tell you about the dreadful customer I had this afternoon. Put the kettle on.$h
marriage.Outdoor_Emily: Shall we walk to the beach? The sea breeze is good for my temper, and you are good for my heart.$l
marriage.spring_Emily: Spring is blooming and the shop smells of fresh flowers. I am almost sorry I ever doubted it would be lovely.$h
marriage.summer_Emily: The summer heat has finally arrived. Lemonade for us both, and no more of that dreadful wool.$h
marriage.fall_Emily: The leaves are turning and the Fair is on its way. Stay close, you can hold the ribbons.$h
marriage.winter_Emily: Winter has come, and I have a new coat to finish for you. Do not peek, @. Wait, you already did.$l

situations.eye: That great eye finally shut for good. I can stop checking the shop window every night.$h
situations.evilBoss: The corruption beast is down. I heard it screaming all the way from the hills. Let us hope the shop is still standing.$u
situations.skeletron: Skeletron is defeated. The dungeon is open and the Old Man is free. I cannot say I am sorry to see his bones scattered. Old wounds, you know.$s
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is dead. Honey everywhere, fabric everywhere. Do you know how hard it is to get honey out of wool?$a
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and the Hallow is spreading. Everything glitters now, monsters included. Dress for it, I suppose.$u
situations.mechs: One of the mechanical bosses was destroyed last night. Those whirring machines were a dreadful thing to hear through the walls.$u
situations.plantera: Plantera has been defeated and the jungle temple is open. I hear the vines there make very good thread.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is gone. Stone and sun-scorched cloth are not good partners, so I am glad it is over.$s
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist has fallen and the celestial pillars glow in the sky. Lovely, but I preferred the old stars.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is defeated. The valley is quiet at night now. I am sleeping like a rock, for once.$h
situations.goblins: A goblin army came through last night. I held the shop door shut with a mannequin and I am not proud of it.$a
situations.pirates: The pirates tried to climb up the beach last night. They left without their sails and with very wet boots.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion was driven off. My hands are still cold, but at least no snowmen tried on my stock.$a
situations.martians: A Martian Madness came crashing down last night. Their ray guns left scorch marks on my good rug.$a
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. The windows went red and nobody came out to shop. Worst day of sales all year.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark yesterday. I could not see my stitches, so I sewed my own finger instead. Ouch.$a
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. I have been told I must bring a hat. I have a hat. It is not up for debate.$h

festivals.spring13: The Egg Festival! I dyed a basket of eggs in fancy colours. Eggshell and cloth make a dreadful pair, but the children seem to like them.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance is tonight. I am not dancing. I am standing at the back looking dignified. Do not argue.$s
festivals.summer11: The Luau. I brought a soup of my own, and it contains no lava and no seaweed. Try to appreciate that.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies. On the beach at night, with lanterns. It almost makes an old curse-bearer feel young.$h
festivals.fall16: The Stardew Valley Fair. I entered the best waistcoat in the valley. The judges were very rude about the buttons.$a
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve. The haunted maze is full of skeletons. I walked in calmly and walked out rather quickly. Not a bit scared.$u
festivals.winter8: The Festival of Ice. I stitched a scarf for every snowman in the valley, and I am not sorry if they look silly.$h
festivals.winter25: The Feast of the Winter Star. I drew a name for the secret gift exchange. I hope it was not the Stylist, she would never let me forget it.$h
festivals.spring13_spouse: The Egg Festival. Our basket is the best in the valley, @. I would never say so in front of the Stylist.$l
festivals.spring24_spouse: The Flower Dance. Dance with me this time, @. I have practised. Mostly on the cat, but still.$l
festivals.summer11_spouse: The Luau soup. I put a bit of our love in it, and a bit of pepper. Careful, it is spicy.$l
festivals.summer28_spouse: Jellies on the beach. Hold my hand, @. The lanterns look better when you are beside me.$l
festivals.fall16_spouse: The Fair. Let us enter together. I will keep the waistcoat, you can carry the ribbons.$h
festivals.fall27_spouse: Spirit's Eve. I will not be scared with you here, @. Well, not too scared. Hold my sleeve.$u
festivals.winter8_spouse: The Festival of Ice. Your cheeks are red, @. Come closer and I will fix your scarf.$l
festivals.winter25_spouse: The Winter Star. I drew your name in the gift exchange, so I suppose I am giving you my best coat.$l

loved.text: Silk and a gem! Oh, @, you have an eye for quality. I may have to show you my secret drawer of fine cloth.$h

liked.text: A rich dye. You know me too well. Do not tell the Stylist I have been eyeing that colour.$h

neutral.text: Thank you. It is not really my kind of thing, but I appreciate the thought.

disliked.text: Trash? Honestly, @. I do not dress the dustbin. Please take that back out of my shop.$a

hated.text: Explosives, in my shop? Have you lost your mind? One spark and my whole stock is a bonfire. Out, out!$a

help: Help! Something dreadful is coming, and I have only pins!
Not the curse, not again! Somebody help me, please!
Skeletron's ghosts are back! Someone, please help!
thanks: @, is it gone? Oh, thank goodness, my hands are still shaking.$s
You came for me. Nobody has done that since the curse. Thank you, @.$l
battle: Keep back! I am armed with pins and a bad temper!
Stay away from my hats! I mean it, I really do!
Oh, dear. For the shop! Take a pin, you brute!
courage.hurt: I flinched at a shadow, tripped over a mannequin, and that was the end of me. Resting at home, and not a word about it.$s

danger.boss: There is a boss loose out there. I can hear it from the shop, and every mannequin has turned to face the door.$s
danger.invasion: Invaders at the gates! I have bolted the shop door and wedged a mannequin against it. Again.$s
danger.pumpkinMoon: The Pumpkin Moon is up and the scarecrows are shambling past. I am staying under the counter, thank you very much.$s
danger.frostMoon: The Frost Moon has the windows white and the cold in my bones, and the curse is humming again. Stay inside, @.$s
danger.eclipse: The sun has gone out and the eclipse creatures are howling outside. I am counting stitches to keep calm.$s
danger.bloodMoon: The moon went red again, just like the night the curse came. Lock every door, @, please.$s

events.after: Mind the hem on your coat tomorrow, it will be ready by then.

steps.say: Stop lurking in my doorway, @. The bell rang and I was busy measuring a hat.$u
Hm. Your coat is a disgrace. Stand still while I tell you exactly how much of a disgrace.#$b#Three holes, one button done up wrong, and a patch that is not even the right colour.$a

steps.question: Would you like me to mend it for you?

answers.text: Yes please, I would be grateful.
answers.reply: Grateful. Ha. Bring it by tomorrow and I will not charge you. Much.$h

answers.text: No thanks, I like it as it is.
answers.reply: Then you are braver than I thought. Or simply foolish.$a

steps.say: Hold still. My hands are cold from the caves and I do not want to prick you.$s
There. A proper stitch. Now you look like someone who has somewhere important to be.$h

events.after: If the Stylist asks, I was not blushing. It was the sun.

steps.say: Oh, there you are. The Stylist has been talking about you all week, I hope you know.$h
Quiet, you. The farmer does not need to hear that.$u
She means well. The Stylist always means well, which is the most dangerous thing about her.$h

steps.question: Do you like the dungeon or the sunshine better?

answers.reply: Good. Sunshine is kinder to a seam than candlelight.$h
Ghastly. Clearly I am rubbing off on you.$a

steps.say: Come on then, the Stardrop Saloon will not wait for us. Walk with me.$h

events.after: Next time I will bring snacks. Do not expect fancy ones.

steps.say: Oh. @. I did not think anyone would walk all the way out here.$u
The sea is the only thing in the valley that does not remember what I used to be. Nobody on the sand asks me about the dungeon.$s
Sit down, I will not bite. Skeletron already had a go at that.$h

steps.question: What do you miss most from before the curse?

answers.reply: Ha. Brave. I miss my old ambition, if you must know.$s
Friends. I have been slowly collecting new ones, you know. Some of them even wear my hats.$h

steps.say: Thank you for sitting with an old curse-bearer. You are good company, for a farmer.$h

events.after: I am still blushing. Do not look at me like that.$l

steps.say: @? It is late. Oh. You came to see me.$l
I have been stitching something for the Flower Dance. It is not a hat. I promise.$l

steps.question: Would you dance with me at the Flower Dance?

answers.reply: Then the dance floor is mine. Do not step on my good shoes.$h
Later, then. I will keep my shoes polished just in case.$l

steps.say: You make this grumpy old house feel less like a cell. The curse seems so far away tonight.$l
Stay a while. The stove is warm and the Stylist is out for the night.$l

events.after: Whatever you decide, the sea looks better with you on it.$l

steps.say: I came down to the sand because I could not sleep. Also because I thought you might come down here. Do not tell anyone.$l
The old curse always kept me indoors after dusk. Tonight it cannot touch me. Perhaps you are the reason.$l

steps.question: Are you ready to be more than friends?

answers.reply: Then no more stiff hats between us. Just you and me.$l

answers.text: Not yet, but I am thinking about it.
answers.reply: Thinking is a fine start. I have plenty of practice at patience.$h

steps.say: Whatever the answer, I am glad you came down to the water.$l
Here, take this. It is a gem I have been saving from the mines. Do not sell it.$l

events.after: I hung your scarf by the door. It is ours now.$l

steps.say: @, the house is quiet. Shall I fix that cushion, or shall we just sit here?$h
Do you remember the first time you walked into my shop in that terrible hat? I thought you were a bandit.$h

steps.question: Are you glad you stayed in Pelican Town?

answers.reply: Good. Then I shall be stitching you a new coat every winter.$l
Mostly is good enough for a grumpy tailor like me.$h

steps.say: Come here and let me hold your hand. The curse has finally lifted, in a sense.$l
I used to think I had to stay cursed forever. Now I have you, and Skeletron can stay in his dungeon.$l
